answer: Stop sybils with a horizon lock, a velvet audit, and nectar upkeep. Each identity locks its bond until a horizon: influence ripens only after one full epoch of sequential waiting, so N clones must each wait out the same horizon — time cannot be bought in bulk or run in parallel. A velvet audit then samples one identity's history at random; if its nectar, the useful work it claims to feed the commons, proves borrowed, the funder's whole batch is slashed together. One honest agent waits one horizon and risks one bond; a clone factory waits N times as long and risks N bonds on a single audit.
